description: F4 cold-start verification item: confirm/address the ~1s cold-start latency noted for the analytics overview route. Per the orchestrator, the 1s hit was dev-mode Turbopack compile; warm p50 is ~25ms. This is largely an observation/verification item. Investigate whether the project already warms critical routes or uses route segment config (export const dynamic / revalidate), and make a change ONLY if there is a concrete, low-risk improvement. Do NOT over-engineer. This feature is independent of FEAT-001 and touches only route-segment config / warming, not aggregation logic.
steps: Search the codebase for existing route warming or segment config: grep for 'export const dynamic', 'export const revalidate', 'export const fetchCache', 'warm', route-warming scripts, and any next.config settings related to caching/prerender. The analytics overview route currently has NO segment config.

Determine the route's dynamic nature: it calls requireTenantCtx() which reads request/session state, so it is inherently dynamic (per-tenant, per-request). Document in findings that the cold-start was dev-mode Turbopack compilation, not a production runtime cost, and that warm p50 is ~25ms.

If and only if there is a concrete low-risk improvement (e.g. the route SHOULD be explicitly marked dynamic to avoid an accidental static-render attempt at build, matching whatever convention sibling tenant API routes already use), apply it consistently with existing sibling routes. If sibling routes do NOT set segment config, do NOT introduce a one-off — instead record the verification finding and make no code change.

Record the conclusion in this feature's findings field: whether a change was made and why, plus the note that a production build (next start) should be used to confirm warm latency (cannot be reliably measured in the sandbox dev server).
acceptance_criteria: A clear written finding documents that the ~1s cold hit was dev-compile and warm p50 is ~25ms, and states whether route warming / segment config already exists in the project.
Either no code change is made (finding-only), OR a low-risk segment-config change is applied consistently with sibling tenant API route conventions and tsc/eslint stay clean.
No over-engineered warming infrastructure is introduced.
verification: export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"; . "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"; nvm use 22 >/dev/null; npx tsc --noEmit
findings:
FINDING-ONLY, NO CODE CHANGE. Investigation of the F4 cold-start item.

1. Cold-start cause: The ~1s hit was dev-mode Turbopack on-demand compilation of the route, not a production runtime cost. Warm p50 is ~25ms. This is a dev-server artifact and disappears once the route is compiled.

2. Route warming infrastructure: NONE exists in the project. Grep for 'warm' only matched the unrelated lead-warming product module (app/tenant/ai/lead-warming, drizzle/schema/lead-warming.ts, lib/lead-warming) and email-warmup features. There is no route-warming script and no next.config prerender/warming setting.

3. Route-segment config convention: NO tenant API route sets segment config. Grep of app/api/tenant/**/*.ts for 'export const dynamic|revalidate|fetchCache|runtime' returned zero matches. The sibling route app/api/tenant/analytics/scheduled-reports/route.ts also calls requireTenantCtx() and sets no segment config. The ONLY routes that set 'export const dynamic' are infrastructure/system routes: app/api/logs/stream (force-dynamic + runtime nodejs), app/api/system/ready (force-dynamic + runtime nodejs), app/api/metrics (force-dynamic), and app/api/openapi (force-static). None are tenant business routes.

4. Dynamic nature: The analytics overview route calls requireTenantCtx() which reads session/request state, so Next.js already infers it as dynamic (per-tenant, per-request). It cannot be accidentally static-rendered at build because it consumes dynamic request APIs, so there is no concrete build-time risk that adding 'export const dynamic = force-dynamic' would mitigate.

CONCLUSION: Adding segment config to only this route would be a one-off inconsistent with every sibling tenant API route, and provides no runtime benefit. Per the plan (step 3: if siblings do NOT set segment config, do NOT introduce a one-off), NO code change was made. Verification: npx tsc --noEmit is clean on the unchanged baseline. Warm latency should be confirmed in a production build via 'next build' + 'next start' (npm run build then next start -p 3099 per pm2 deploy), since the sandbox dev server (Turbopack on-demand compile) is not a reliable place to measure warm p50.
